instantiated_cells.justification: The statute requires principals (not lobbyists) to file periodic expense statements, while lobbyists only provide signed information to the principal for inclusion in the principal’s filing, so there is no separate lobbyist-filed spending report.
The only periodic spending disclosure specified is the principal’s expense statement due July 31 and January 31 (semiannual), not an annual lobbyist spending report.
No provision requires lobbyists to file monthly spending reports; the periodic filing duty is imposed on principals semiannually.
The statute sets semiannual principal expense statements and does not establish any quarterly lobbyist spending report.

Although principal expense statements are filed semiannually, the lobbyist is not the named filer of a separate spending report, so the lobbyist spending-report cadence does not include semiannual filings.
There is no triannual spending report required of lobbyists; reporting duties are structured around principal filings.
The statute does not impose any other-periodic spending report filed by lobbyists; only principals file the periodic expense statements.
Aggregate total lobbying expenditures are reported in the principal’s expense statement, not in a spending report filed by the lobbyist.

Compensation to lobbyists for lobbying is included in the principal’s reported lobbying expenditures, but lobbyists are not required to file their own compensation totals in a separate lobbyist spending report.
The law requires the principal to list payments to each lobbyist exceeding $200 during the reporting period, but it does not require a lobbyist-filed report breaking compensation down by payer.
Office overhead and other indirect lobbying costs are disclosed by principals in their expense statements, not by lobbyists in a separate spending report.

The statute broadly prohibits lobbyists/principals from furnishing lodging/transportation/food/things of value and requires principals to report certain reimbursements, but it does not require a lobbyist-filed spending report disclosing such items.
The required expense statement is filed by the principal and reports aggregate totals and some listings (e.g., lobbyist payments), but there is no lobbyist-filed report requiring itemized expenses.
Lobbyists provide supporting information to principals for the principal’s filing, but the statute does not require lobbyists to file an itemized spending report themselves.
Any categorization of expenditures appears in the principal’s expense statement requirements rather than in a separate spending report filed by lobbyists.
Identification of proposals/topics is a reporting duty imposed on principals, not a requirement in a lobbyist-filed periodic spending report.
The statute requires principals to report topics/legislative proposals with reasonable specificity, but it does not require lobbyists to file a spending report disclosing general subject matter.
While principals must report each legislative proposal/proposed administrative rule number/budget bill subject or topic, this requirement is not part of a lobbyist-filed periodic spending report.
Specific identifiers (legislative proposal and proposed administrative rule numbers) are reported by principals under §13.67(1), not by lobbyists in a periodic spending report.
The principal must report the proposal/topic being lobbied but the statute does not require (and does not create a lobbyist spending report to include) the lobbyist’s position on a bill.
The principal must estimate proportion of time spent per proposal/topic, but there is no lobbyist-filed spending report requiring expenditures per issue.
Principals must keep a daily time record that includes meeting with officials, but the statute does not require lobbyists to file a report listing contacts made.
Lobbyists provide identifying information on a license application, but the statute does not require a lobbyist periodic spending report that includes the lobbyist’s address/phone.

A lobbyist or principal must file written authorization for the lobbyist to represent the principal, but this is not a lobbyist spending report requiring the lobbyist to disclose all principals represented in a periodic spending filing.

Principal registration statements filed by principals include the principal’s name and business address, but lobbyists are not required to file a periodic spending report including principal contact information.
The nature/purpose/business activity of the principal is disclosed on the principal’s registration statement, not on a lobbyist-filed periodic spending report.

The periodic expense statement requirement applies to registered principals regardless of activity level, but there is no separate lobbyist spending report that could require a 'no activity' filing by lobbyists.

The statute does not require a lobbyist spending report at all and does not define its scope to include household members of officials; the only household reference concerns an exception to prohibited-value rules, not reporting.

unscoreable_emissions.justification: Because no separate lobbyist spending report is required, there is no 'other' lobbyist spending-report cadence to specify.
